gold.reasoning: 1. Castleman disease — “Castleman disease was considered but excluded after a further biopsy and review by several expert histopathologists.” 2. Hyper-IgD syndrome — “Mutations were not found in the coding regions of MVK … making the diagnoses of Hyper IgD syndrome … unlikely.” 3. Schnitzler syndrome — “It was first described by L. Schnitzler, as a clinical entity consisting of chronic urticaria, fever, bone pain, arthralgia or arthritis, and a monoclonal IgM gammopathy.”

source_issues: s019 records a tentative diagnosis of adult-onset Still's disease, which differs from the gold label (Schnitzler syndrome); the second-look note calls it a distractor.
notes: Index visit: the clinic presentation six months after the first visit, when he reported generalized fatigue, daily fevers, night sweats, arthralgias with right knee and tibial pain, weight loss and axillary and inguinal lymphadenopathy (s006, s007), followed by the inpatient workup (s008–s018). The first clinic visit (s001–s005) is history: its tests are findings labelled as six months earlier. This later visit is chosen because the selection notes rest the diagnosis on fevers, bone pain and arthralgia after the urticaria, which appear only at this visit; framed at the first visit the case would have only urticaria and a small paraprotein.
The selection note does not say explicitly that a later visit is the best framing; the choice follows its screen and second-look reasons.
No physical examination is reported in the prompt.
